name: Generator Installation
metaTitle: Generator Installation in Broward | Ghost Crown
metaDescription: Generator installation in Broward County by a licensed master electrician. We assess your service and what you need to keep running, then quote it right. Book.
intro: Down here, the power going out is not a rare event. It is part of life in South Florida, and anyone who has been through a long outage knows the feeling. A generator is how you take that worry off the table. It is not about running the whole house like nothing happened. It is about keeping the essentials on, the things that matter when the grid goes down. But a generator is only as good as the electrical work behind it, and the honest first question is always the same one we ask before any big load: what can your service actually support, and what do you truly need to keep running? We answer that in person, before we promise anything. Then we give you one honest price for the job that fits your home.

definition.heading: What is generator installation
definition.body: Generator installation is the work of adding a backup power source to a home or commercial property so that when the grid goes down, the power you depend on most stays on. A generator on its own is just an engine and an alternator. The part that makes it safe and useful is the electrical work around it: a proper connection to your electrical system through a transfer switch that keeps generator power and grid power safely separated, sized and installed so it carries the loads you have chosen without overloading anything. That is where a licensed electrician matters. The install is not simply setting a machine in the yard. It is tying that machine into your home's electrical service correctly, so it powers what you need when you need it and does so without creating a new hazard in the process.

symptoms.title: Outages that keep leaving you in the dark
symptoms.body: The power goes out often enough that you have stopped being surprised by it. Each time you are counting hours and hoping it comes back before the food turns. A generator is how you stop living at the mercy of the grid.

symptoms.title: Medical equipment that cannot lose power
symptoms.body: Someone in the home relies on equipment or refrigerated medication that has to stay running. An outage is not an inconvenience in that case, it is a real risk, and reliable backup power is worth having in place before the next storm season.

symptoms.title: A refrigerator and freezer full of food
symptoms.body: A long outage means watching a full refrigerator and freezer slowly warm up and throwing the loss away. Keeping those essentials cold through an outage is one of the most common reasons homeowners here decide a generator is worth it.

symptoms.title: A home office you cannot afford to lose
symptoms.body: You work from home and a dead grid means dead work: no internet, no computer, no way to do your job. For a household that depends on staying connected, backup power for the essentials keeps the day from falling apart.

symptoms.title: A commercial property that cannot go dark
symptoms.body: Downtime costs your business real money, or your tenants expect the lights and systems to stay on. Commercial backup power raises the same core questions as a home, at a larger scale, and it starts with assessing the service.

symptoms.title: Essential systems that fail without power
symptoms.body: A pool pump, a well, a sump, or another system quietly stops the moment the grid does, and that can create its own problems. If losing power means more than just darkness for your property, a generator earns its place.

process.body: You call and we talk about your property, your history with outages, and what you most need to keep running when the power drops. That conversation shapes everything that follows and tells you what to expect before we come out. No pressure, no script.

process.title: One honest price for the job that fits
process.body: From what we saw and what you told us, we forecast the work and give you one price for a system matched to your home. If the electrical service needs attention first, we tell you plainly, once, and let you decide. We price it once and we price it right.

process.title: The in-house crew does the install
process.body: Our own crew sets the generator, installs the transfer switch, and ties it into your electrical system correctly, so grid power and generator power stay safely separated. The same people who priced the job do the work, with the owner on it from start to finish.

process.title: Permit, inspection, and a follow-up
process.body: Generator work is permitted and inspected, and we handle that: the permit is pulled and the owner meets the inspector in person. Once it passes, we walk you through how it runs and follow up so you know exactly what to expect the next time the grid goes down.

benefits.title: The essentials stay on
benefits.body: When the grid drops, the power you depend on most keeps running. Not a promise to run the whole house like nothing happened, but a real plan to keep what matters alive through an outage.

benefits.title: Honest sizing, assessed in person
benefits.body: What a generator can carry depends on your service and the install, so we work that out on your property before anything is promised. You get a system matched to your home, not an optimistic guess.

benefits.title: Tied in safely by a master electrician
benefits.body: A transfer switch keeps generator power and grid power separated the way code requires, protecting your home and anyone working on the lines. This is exactly where a licensed install earns its keep.

benefits.title: Peace of mind before the next season
benefits.body: You stop dreading the forecast and the flicker of the lights. Knowing the essentials will stay on is the quiet confidence a generator is really for, and it is what you are paying for.

localSections.heading: Older services and the load a generator asks for
localSections.body: Broward County homes come from many eras, and the electrical service in an older home was sized for the life that home was expected to live, not for a backup power system tied into it decades later. Adding a generator, and the transfer switch that makes it safe, is a meaningful addition to your electrical system, and it has to work with the service you already have. Some panels are in fine shape for it. Others, especially the older problem-brand panels found around South Florida, raise questions that have to be answered first. This is why the assessment comes before any promise. We look at what your service can actually support and how a generator would tie into it, and if the panel or service needs attention before the generator makes sense, we tell you plainly. A backup system is only as reliable as the electrical work behind it, so we start with that work, not with the machine.

localSections.heading: Heat, humidity, and hurricane season are the reason
localSections.body: The reason generators matter here is the same reason South Florida is hard on equipment: the weather. Long, hot summers, heavy humidity, and a hurricane season that reliably tests the grid every year. Outages are simply a fact of life in this climate, and when they come they can last. A generator installed here also has to live in that same environment, usually outdoors, in heat and humidity and, near the coast, salt air. That reality shapes how the work is done: proper connections, hardware suited to an outdoor South Florida location, and an install built to hold up season after season, not just to pass on day one. When we plan a generator for your property, we are planning for the conditions it will actually face, because a backup system that fails when you finally need it is worse than no plan at all.

localSections.heading: Permits, inspections, and the transfer switch
localSections.body: Generator installation is electrical work that Broward County building departments expect to see permitted and inspected, and for good reason. The heart of a safe install is the transfer switch, the device that keeps generator power and utility power from ever meeting. Without it, a generator can backfeed power onto the grid and put utility workers and your own home at serious risk. That is not a corner anyone should cut, and the permit and inspection exist to confirm it was done right. We pull the permit where it is required and the owner meets the inspector in person, because the person who did the work should answer for it. When the inspection passes, you have an independent confirmation that your backup power is tied in safely and a clean record on the property, which matters if you ever sell or file a claim.

localSections.heading: What insurance carriers think about backup power
localSections.body: Florida insurance carriers pay close attention to how electrical work on a home was done and whether it was permitted, and a generator is a significant, visible addition to a property's electrical system. An unpermitted or amateur generator install is exactly the kind of thing that can complicate a claim or raise questions at renewal. We are not trying to worry anyone. The simple truth is that a licensed installation with the permit on record is the version that holds up when it is examined. When a master electrician does the work, pulls the permit, and passes the inspection, you have documentation that the system was added correctly and safely. In a state where carriers have grown cautious, that record is worth having. Doing it properly the first time is the least expensive path over the life of the home, which is why we never cut corners to win the job.

guide.title: The honest guide to installing a generator in South Florida

sections.heading: What a generator install actually involves
sections.body: When people picture a generator, they picture the machine. The machine is the easy part. What makes a generator safe and genuinely useful is the electrical work that ties it into your home, and that is where a licensed master electrician matters. A proper install means connecting the generator to your electrical system through a transfer switch, the device that keeps generator power and grid power completely separated so the two can never meet. It means sizing the connection and the loads so the generator carries what you have chosen without being overwhelmed. And it means doing all of that to code, with a permit and an inspection, so the system is safe for your family and for the utility workers out on the lines during an outage. Setting a machine in the yard is not the job. Tying it into your service correctly is the job, and it is the part that decides whether your backup power is a comfort or a hazard.

sections.heading: Outages are a fact of life here
sections.body: In South Florida, planning for the power to go out is not pessimism, it is realism. Hurricane season tests the grid every year, summer storms knock out neighborhoods, and when an outage comes it can stretch from hours into days. A generator is how a household stops being helpless in that stretch. It is worth being clear about what a generator is for, though. For most homes it is not about running everything as if nothing happened. It is about keeping the essentials on: the refrigerator and freezer full of food, the medical equipment someone depends on, the internet for a home office, a pump or a system that causes trouble the moment it stops. Deciding what counts as essential for your home is one of the first conversations we have, because that answer shapes the whole install. A generator built around what you actually need is the one that earns its cost when the lights finally go out.

sections.heading: Sizing honestly: what you can really run
sections.body: This is the part where honesty separates a good installer from a salesperson, and it works exactly like our approach to EV chargers. What a generator can run is not a number we pull from a brochure. It depends on your electrical service, the install, and the specific loads you want to keep alive. A generator has a limit, and asking it to carry more than it should does not end well. So before we promise anything, we assess your service in person and talk through your priorities: what has to stay on, what would be nice to keep, and what can wait until the grid returns. From that we can be honest about what a given setup will and will not carry for your property. We would rather tell you plainly that a certain plan will cover your essentials but not your whole house than let you believe something that turns out to be false during the one week a year you truly need it. Assessment before promise. Every time.

sections.heading: The transfer switch, and why it is not optional
sections.body: If there is one part of a generator install you should never let anyone skip or shortcut, it is the transfer switch. Its job is simple and critical: it makes sure your home is drawing from either the grid or the generator, never both at once. Without a proper transfer switch, a generator can push power backward onto the utility lines, a condition called backfeed. That is dangerous in two directions. It can injure or kill a utility worker who believes the line is dead, and it can damage your own home and generator when grid power returns. This is exactly why generator work is permitted and inspected, and why it belongs in the hands of a licensed electrician rather than a weekend project. A transfer switch installed correctly is invisible in daily life. You will likely never think about it. But it is the single component that turns a generator from a hazard into a safe, dependable backup, and we do not treat it as anything less.

sections.heading: What the day of installation looks like
sections.body: On install day, our own in-house crew handles the work from start to finish. We set the generator in its place, install the transfer switch, and tie the system into your electrical service so grid power and generator power stay safely separated. We account for the South Florida environment the equipment will live in, with proper connections and hardware suited to heat, humidity, and, near the coast, salt air. Generator installs vary in size, so the timeline depends on the scope, and we tell you what to expect before we begin rather than leaving you guessing. If the electrical service needs work before the generator, we will have told you that at the assessment, not sprung it on you mid-job. Throughout, the owner is on the work, because the person who priced it should be the one standing behind it. Before we call it done, we walk you through how the system runs so you know exactly what happens the next time the grid goes down.

sections.heading: An honest word about cost
sections.body: We are going to be straight with you here, because that is how we do everything. Generator work is quoted per property after an on-site assessment, and we do not publish a price for it, because an honest price does not exist until we have seen your service and understood what you need to keep running. The scope of a generator job varies widely from one home to the next, and anyone who quotes you a firm number over the phone, before looking at your electrical system, is guessing. We would rather come out, look at the real thing, and give you one honest, forecast-based price for a system that fits your home. If your electrical service needs attention before the generator makes sense, we tell you that plainly, once, and let you decide. Price it once, price it right. That is the whole philosophy, and it protects you from the surprises that come with a lowball number and a pile of change orders.

sections.heading: How to choose the contractor who installs it
sections.body: A generator is a serious addition to your home, and the electrical work behind it is what keeps it safe, so choose the installer with care. Ask whether they are licensed. Ghost Crown Electric is a Florida Certified Electrical Contractor with statewide authority and a Broward County Master Electrician, with 286 permitted projects on public record and ten years of showing up when we said we would. Ask whether they will pull a permit and have the transfer switch and connection inspected, because anyone willing to skip that is skipping the part that keeps a generator from becoming a danger. Ask who does the work, an in-house crew or a rotating set of subs. And listen for honesty about sizing and about your service, because an installer who will tell you the truth about what a generator can and cannot carry is one who will be honest with you about everything else. We stay in our lane, we do the work right, and we let a decade of doing it that way speak for us.

faqs.answer: That depends on your electrical service, the install, and the loads you choose to keep on, which is why we assess it in person before promising anything. For most homes a generator is about keeping the essentials alive, the refrigerator, medical equipment, internet, key systems, rather than running the entire house. We tell you honestly what a given setup will and will not carry.

Generator jobs vary widely from home to home. We come out, look at the real thing, and give you one honest price for a system that fits.

faqs.question: Do I need a permit for a generator?
faqs.answer: Yes. Generator installation is electrical work that Broward County building departments expect to see permitted and inspected, in large part because the transfer switch must be done correctly for safety. We pull the permit where it is required and the owner meets the inspector in person, so the work is on record and confirmed safe, which also protects you if you ever sell or file a claim.

faqs.question: Why does the transfer switch matter so much?
faqs.answer: The transfer switch keeps your home drawing from either the grid or the generator, never both. Without it, a generator can push power back onto the utility lines, which can injure a lineworker who thinks the line is dead and damage your own home when grid power returns. It is the single component that makes backup power safe, and we never shortcut it.

faqs.question: Will a generator protect me during hurricane season?
faqs.answer: A properly installed generator keeps your chosen essentials running when the grid goes down, which in South Florida happens most reliably during storm season. It is about keeping the important things on through an outage, not about anything beyond that. We size and install it around what your home actually needs, and we assess your service in person before we promise what it will carry.

faqs.question: Do you install generators for commercial properties?
faqs.answer: Yes, for both homes and commercial properties across Broward County. A commercial job raises the same core questions as a home, whether the service can support the system and what has to stay running, just at a larger scale. We assess the property in person, forecast the work, and give you one honest price quoted for your specific building.
